# d3k

> A managed browser and a bounded server/browser event timeline for coding agents.

d3k is written in TypeScript and runs under Node.js 24+. Install its skill with
`pnpm dlx skills add vercel-labs/dev3000 --skill d3k`, then ask your agent to run
and debug your project. No global CLI installation is required for skill use.

The same runtime backs d3k, dev3000, and d3k-runtime. Commands:
- start: own the dev server and project browser in a retained process
- status: report readiness, session ID, and event cursor
- events: read events after a cursor, with source/level filters
- logs and errors: recent views over the live event timeline
- browser: drive the exact monitored browser via agent-browser and CDP
- stop: close the app and browser
- portless status/setup: prepare canonical port-free local HTTPS
- sandbox: run a Vercel project remotely with a local Chrome browser
- mcp: serve local stdio MCP tools to ChatGPT or Claude Desktop; --print-config prints absolute-path setup
- upgrade: explicitly update the global package with Bun

Local and sandbox startup require canonical Portless HTTPS on the laptop. Local apps use https://my-app.localhost; sandbox apps use https://<project>.d3k.localhost (override with --hostname). The loopback companion streams app traffic to a session-token-protected sandbox endpoint.
Use start --command for custom dev commands; timeout flags use milliseconds.
The browser profile persists authentication. Events remain in bounded memory
(5,000 events or 8 MiB) and disappear on exit. Cursor responses report resets
and dropped evidence. Request bodies and headers are omitted; URL query values
are redacted. Server and console text may still contain application secrets.

Capture screenshots explicitly with browser screenshot <absolute-path>.
There is no terminal dashboard, automatic screenshot/screencast capture,
file-backed logging, tmux agent launcher, skill installer, or automatic upgrade.

Sandbox mode requires Vercel CLI login, Bun, and local Chrome. The linked repo,
Development env and dev server live remotely; no local checkout is needed.
The assistant can run locally in a terminal harness or desktop MCP client.
A persistent authenticated outbound WSS bridge carries CDP between the local
browser and sandbox. Public repo creation is supported; private repos require
an existing sandbox containing the checkout and --attach.
The public sandbox app endpoint requires a session token supplied by the loopback companion. Application authentication remains the app's responsibility.

Source: https://github.com/vercel-labs/dev3000

Sandbox resume: `d3k --resume` lists locally saved session IDs, projects, sandbox names, branches, URLs, and last-used times. `d3k --resume <id>` restores that sandbox checkout and hostname, refreshes Development env and dependencies, restarts the dev runtime, and pairs the retained browser profile using fresh bridge/proxy tokens. No repository checkout is needed on the laptop. Ctrl-C closes the browser and prints the resume command to stdout. Saved entries contain discovery metadata, not credentials or past terminal output; remote availability is checked on resume. Optional `--command`, `--hostname`, `--timeout`, `--no-shell`, `--no-fx`, `--no-gateway`, `--gateway-budget`, and `--headless` override launch settings. Sandboxes originally created by d3k stop compute again on resumed exit; externally attached sandboxes remain running.

Optional --harness fx|codex|claude launches a supported coding harness after readiness, locally with start or --project. With --project, local is the default harness location; --harness-location sandbox selects the remote harness. Resume remembers the location. The local harness uses a temporary control directory with remote file/shell/log tools and direct local Chrome tools, without a local project checkout or saved env file. Codex/Claude receive per-launch MCP configuration; fx also has an explicit remote-command helper. sandbox_github publishes Git objects, branches and PRs for the linked repository through local gh authentication without forwarding credentials. Tool outputs and harness history may contain code the agent reads. It requires an interactive terminal and supplies d3k skill context; arbitrary commands are rejected.

Sandbox security: macOS is currently required. The local Chrome browser and its children run under an OS filesystem policy allowing system files, Chrome, and the dedicated session profile and temporary files; other laptop files are denied. This outer policy replaces Chrome’s inner sandbox because macOS cannot nest them. Browser profile and authenticated web sessions remain accessible to sandbox automation. Sandbox fx automatically receives a project-scoped Gateway key with a $5 non-renewing session budget including BYOK usage, and automatic expiration after --timeout minutes (default: 60, shared with sandbox compute). d3k prints the key expiration time on exit. Resume creates a fresh key. Use --gateway-budget to change the limit or --no-gateway for manual authentication. Project code shares access to this key; use trusted projects. Vercel management tokens and laptop harness credentials stay local.

Desktop MCP: d3k mcp serves local stdio; d3k mcp --print-config prints mcpServers.d3k with absolute Node/CLI paths and PATH, without credentials. Configure in ChatGPT Desktop MCP settings or Claude Desktop local mcpServers (not a remote connector or Cowork). The server supplies workflow instructions. sandbox_sessions lists resume IDs; sandbox_start accepts project or resume and returns starting; poll sandbox_status until ready before sandbox_exec/read_file/write_file/runtime/browser/github. sandbox_stop returns stopping; wait for stopped. One active session per server. Disconnecting the server closes Chrome and d3k-owned compute while preserving remote files and resume metadata. No terminal harness or Gateway key is created. Project code/env stay remote; desktop tool history can contain read source. Requires macOS, local Vercel login, Bun, Node 24+, Sandbox access and canonical Portless.

Recovery for desktop MCP and local sandbox harnesses: sandbox_recover action=start restores a stopped/unhealthy dev runtime and browser bridge in the existing sandbox, preserving the agent, local Chrome and remote edits. Poll action=status until recovered or failed, then reread sandbox_runtime status and reproduce because restarted runtimes lose old in-memory evidence. It does not clone, reinstall dependencies, replay agent commands, renew Gateway keys or extend compute lifetime. A confirmed runtime exit keeps these connections alive for explicit recovery.
